english: Let $a$, $b$ and $c$ be real numbers with $c>0$, and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by
If $f$ is differentiable at every point of $\mathbb{R}$, then the value of $f(3)-f(1)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$, $b$ तथा $c$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं जहाँ $c>0$ है, तथा $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ निम्न द्वारा परिभाषित है
यदि $f$, $\mathbb{R}$ के प्रत्येक बिन्दु पर अवकलनीय है, तो $f(3)-f(1)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Let $q(x)=x^{4}-8x^{2}+4x$. Differentiability at $x=c$ and $x=-c$ needs $q'(c)=a=q'(-c)$ and $q(\pm c)=\pm ac+b$
(The line $y=4x-16$ touches the quartic at both $x=\pm2$.) Since $1<2\le3$: $f(1)=a+b=-12$, $f(3)=81-72+12=21$
solution_full: Let $q(x)=x^{4}-8x^{2}+4x$, so $q'(x)=4x^{3}-16x+4$. Inside $(-c,c)$, $f$ is the line $ax+b$; outside, $f=q$. Both pieces are differentiable, so only the junctions $x=c$ and $x=-c$ matter.
At $x=c$: continuity needs $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to c^{-}}f(x)=ac+b=q(c)$, and equal one-sided derivatives need $a=q'(c)$. At $x=-c$: $-ac+b=q(-c)$ and $a=q'(-c)$.
Geometrically, the line $y=4x-16$ is tangent to $y=q(x)$ at both $x=-2$ and $x=2$: indeed $q(x)-(4x-16)=(x^{2}-4)^{2}$.
originality_note: New: a piecewise function in which a line replaces the quartic between -c and c; differentiability at both junctions forces the line to be the double tangent of the quartic, which fixes c, a and b together (way 3). Closest known: piecewise functions with a line and a polynomial, where a and b are found from continuity and differentiability at one known point. Different because: the junction c is unknown and symmetric junctions give four conditions whose consistency is the point.
blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving non uniformly defined functions
Continuity and Differentiability of functions involving non uniformly defined functions

concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving non unifor: The one-sided limits of f and of its difference quotient at x = c and x = -c give q(c) = ac + b and a = q'(c) (and the same at -c).
concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: Differentiability of the piecewise f at both junctions forces q'(c) = q'(-c), hence c = 2, a = 4, b = -16.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy/mpmath and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that the four junction conditions are consistent and give a unique (a, b, c) with c > 0, that 1 lies inside and 3 outside (-c, c), and that f(3) - f(1) = 33 is a positive 2-digit integer (direct evaluation). Changed: No change.
key_step: Equating q'(c) and q'(-c) to find c = 2 (double tangent), then a and b.
justification: Two linked ideas: four junction conditions with an unknown junction, then evaluation on the correct pieces; no options. Comparable to the piecewise continuity/differentiability anchor 2024-P1-Q17 (L3).
